Assemble and validate input data

Source: R/data.R
bruce_data.Rd

The data contract of the package. Everything specific to a city enters here: which networks exist, which ones are trusted, and where the stations are.

Usage

bruce_data(obs, stations, sources, crs, background = NULL, background_sd = 0.7)

Arguments

obs

Data frame of station observations with columns station_id, date (coercible to Date) and value (e.g. daily median or maximum temperature).

stations

Data frame with one row per station: station_id, source, and either x/y in crs or lon/lat in WGS84.

sources

Data frame describing each network, with columns

  • source: network name, matching stations$source;

  • bias: FALSE for reference networks (e.g. official stations), TRUE for networks that get an estimated offset (low-cost sensors, citizen stations, airports with a known systematic difference);

  • obs_sd: fixed observation standard deviation, or NA to estimate it with a PC prior. At least one reference network (bias = FALSE) is needed to identify the intercept.

crs

Projected coordinate reference system in metres (EPSG code or anything accepted by sf::st_crs()).

background

Optional gridded product on the same variable (e.g. ERA5-Land daily statistic), as a data frame with date, value and x/y or lon/lat of cell centres. Enters as an additional unbiased likelihood with fixed standard deviation background_sd.

background_sd

Fixed observation standard deviation of the background.

Value

An object of class bruce_data.
